memorycache-size-expiration-policy.title: Design MemoryCache size and expiration policies
memorycache-size-expiration-policy.short: Bound cache lifetime and memory instead of growing forever
memorycache-size-expiration-policy.summary: IMemoryCache supports per-entry expiration and size accounting so in-process caches can have explicit lifetime and memory policies.
memorycache-size-expiration-policy.why: Caching can remove repeated work, but unbounded entries can retain stale data and consume increasing memory.
memorycache-size-expiration-policy.tips: Choose a SizeLimit that reflects real entry cost and select absolute or sliding expiration according to the data contract.

partitioned-rate-limiter-resource-keys.title: Partition rate limits by users or resource keys
partitioned-rate-limiter-resource-keys.short: Give each logical key an independent limiter
partitioned-rate-limiter-resource-keys.summary: PartitionedRateLimiter derives a partition key from a request and applies a limiter associated with that user, API key, or resource.
partitioned-rate-limiter-resource-keys.why: Partitioning can align fairness and resource protection with actual tenants instead of forcing every request through one global quota.
partitioned-rate-limiter-resource-keys.tips: Avoid attacker-controlled unbounded partition growth and define queueing and rejection behavior explicitly.

gc-memory-pressure-native-allocations.title: Report large native allocations as GC memory pressure
gc-memory-pressure-native-allocations.short: Tell the GC about significant memory held outside the managed heap
gc-memory-pressure-native-allocations.summary: GC.AddMemoryPressure and RemoveMemoryPressure let wrappers report substantial unmanaged memory that is otherwise invisible to managed heap size.
gc-memory-pressure-native-allocations.why: A tiny managed wrapper can own a huge native allocation, causing the GC to underestimate the process memory pressure.
gc-memory-pressure-native-allocations.tips: Report only meaningful unmanaged ownership, pair additions with removals, and do not call these APIs for every tiny allocation.

socketasynceventargs-reuse.title: Reuse SocketAsyncEventArgs in high-throughput networking
socketasynceventargs-reuse.short: Reuse socket operation state and buffers across requests
socketasynceventargs-reuse.summary: SocketAsyncEventArgs provides a reusable operation object for socket I/O, reducing per-operation allocation in high-throughput servers.
socketasynceventargs-reuse.why: Small allocations multiplied across many connections can create significant GC pressure.
socketasynceventargs-reuse.tips: Prefer simpler modern Socket async APIs unless measurements justify the complexity, and handle synchronous completion and ownership carefully.

iasyncdisposable-dual-dispose-pattern.title: Implement IAsyncDisposable as a resource-lifetime contract
iasyncdisposable-dual-dispose-pattern.short: Coordinate asynchronous cleanup with normal disposal responsibilities
iasyncdisposable-dual-dispose-pattern.summary: Resources that require asynchronous cleanup can implement IAsyncDisposable so await using waits for their release to finish.
iasyncdisposable-dual-dispose-pattern.why: Blocking on asynchronous flushes can stall threads, while abandoning cleanup can lose buffered data or leave resources open.
iasyncdisposable-dual-dispose-pattern.tips: When supporting both disposal forms, share cleanup safely without double disposal and follow the full pattern for inheritable types.

regex-source-generator-hot-path.title: Generate fixed regular expressions with GeneratedRegex
regex-source-generator-hot-path.short: Generate regex implementation code at build time
regex-source-generator-hot-path.summary: GeneratedRegexAttribute generates an implementation for a fixed regular expression during compilation.
regex-source-generator-hot-path.why: Frequently used fixed patterns can avoid runtime parsing or dynamic-code dependencies and work well with AOT deployment.
regex-source-generator-hot-path.tips: It does not fit dynamic patterns; benchmark performance cases and do not replace simple character searches with regex unnecessarily.

threadpool-starvation-blocking-async.title: Avoid ThreadPool starvation from blocking async work
threadpool-starvation-blocking-async.short: Do not occupy pool threads with Result or Wait on asynchronous I/O
threadpool-starvation-blocking-async.summary: Synchronously blocking on asynchronous operations can consume ThreadPool workers that are needed to run the continuations completing those same operations.
threadpool-starvation-blocking-async.why: Under server load, blocked workers can cause rising latency and a feedback loop of more queued work and more blocking.
threadpool-starvation-blocking-async.tips: Propagate await through the call chain and treat truly synchronous APIs and CPU parallelism as separate design problems.

json-unknown-derived-type-contract.title: Define behavior for unknown derived JSON types
json-unknown-derived-type-contract.short: Treat unknown type discriminators as an explicit compatibility contract
json-unknown-derived-type-contract.summary: Polymorphic JSON can receive future or invalid type discriminators, so applications should deliberately define how unknown derived types behave.
json-unknown-derived-type-contract.why: Explicit behavior avoids accidental fallback or confusing failures when producer and consumer versions differ.
json-unknown-derived-type-contract.tips: Whitelist allowed derived types for untrusted input and test any fallback policy required for forward compatibility.

unity-nativearray-job-data.title: Pass data to Unity Jobs with NativeArray
unity-nativearray-job-data.short: Use contiguous job-compatible memory with explicit lifetime
unity-nativearray-job-data.summary: NativeArray provides contiguous unmanaged storage designed to participate in Unity's Job System safety and scheduling model.
unity-nativearray-job-data.why: Large data-oriented workloads can be split into jobs without traversing many managed objects and with memory layouts suited to parallel processing.
unity-nativearray-job-data.tips: Respect the selected Allocator lifetime and never dispose storage before all dependent JobHandles complete.

async-local-execution-context-cost.title: Understand AsyncLocal and ExecutionContext propagation cost
async-local-execution-context-cost.short: Keep implicit async context small on hot paths
async-local-execution-context-cost.summary: AsyncLocal values flow with ExecutionContext across asynchronous work, making them useful for request-scoped ambient context.
async-local-execution-context-cost.why: Frequent changes and many ambient values add work around async boundaries and can hide dependencies that ordinary parameters make explicit.
async-local-execution-context-cost.tips: Reserve ambient context for values that truly need propagation and pass ordinary application data explicitly when practical.
